personas.name: abnormal-benign-trabeculation-prostatic-enlargement-minor-complete
personas.description: Flexible cystoscopy for lower urinary tract symptoms in an elderly male finds mild bladder wall trabeculation and prostatic enlargement, both benign structural findings: no tumour, inflammation, stones, or stricture — this grades minor severity via the dedicated benign-structural rule, classified as abnormal (not normal) since these are genuine structured findings; report complete — expect abnormal classification + minor severity + 100% completeness + recommended follow-up (per local surveillance guidance) + routine-follow-up.

state.clinicalHistory: Lower urinary tract symptoms in an elderly male; flexible cystoscopy for further assessment.
state.findingsNarrative: Mild bladder wall trabeculation consistent with longstanding bladder outflow obstruction, and mild prostatic enlargement narrowing the prostatic urethra. No tumour, inflammation, stones, or stricture.
state.impression: Benign bladder trabeculation and prostatic enlargement consistent with bladder outflow obstruction; no tumour or other significant pathology.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Refer to urology for consideration of BPH management; no further cystoscopic surveillance required for this finding alone.
